description: Sixty anonymous inferred roofs on the already modelled North Division ground between the north bank, Kinzie Street, and Michigan Street, and since T-1205 six trade roofs on the north face of Kinzie Street (sequences 61-66). Since T-1746, 26 ordinary dwellings carried off Kinzie's Addition's two subdivided blocks into the three clusters south of Michigan Street (sequences 68-93). These are production slots, not recovered buildings or recovered lots.

coordinate_basis.note: The 25 m value is a placement-control radius, not evidence for any anonymous roof. The Wright affine has 17.5 m RMS and the anonymous lot selection adds unquantified error; every placement remains conjectural.

extent.extension_note: Extend the terrain, water mask, North Branch bank traces, flora zones, and collision heightfield together from N +400 to at least N +760 before placing roofs north of Michigan Street. Ohio Street control lies near N +633; the extra 127 m provides a complete outer block and visible open prairie rather than ending the world on a street. Keep E +1700: it already clears the 1834 lake shore. Do not extend west for this North parcel; Wabansia and the west side of the North Branch require a separately traced hydrology parcel.

placement_constraints: Reject any footprint whose sampled terrain cell is water; proximity to North Water Street never overrides the authoritative water mask.
Sample one visible/collision heightfield for foundations, structures, and vegetation. No hidden flat placement plane is permitted.
Reserve a minimum 25 m review buffer around every named structure footprint unless the anonymous roof is explicitly assigned to a documented rear yard by later research.
Reserve the Fort Dearborn military compound and the Lake House construction yard; anonymous infill must not overlap either.
Do not interpret a cadastral lot line as evidence that a roof existed. Empty frontage is an affirmative reconstruction requirement.
A newly documented named North Division roof substitutes for the closest anonymous family and inventory class; it does not increase the 665-roof total.
Run polygon collision, terrain coverage, water-mask, and existing-structure exclusion tests before converting this recipe into structure records.

migrated.why: THE SAME 60 ROOFS STAND AND NINE OF THEM ARE CALLED SOMETHING ELSE. T-1445 adjudicated the town's 285 anonymous roofs and returned 32 refamily verdicts; T-1451 carried out the six whose ids do not move. These nine are the North Division's, and `generate_north_infill` builds a record's id out of its family and sequence, so refamilying one RENAMES it and every committed file that names it --- the sidecars, the liberties, the signage and trade goods, the lodging model and the lodgers seated under two of these roofs, the reconstructed seating, the business layer and the boarding house authored over `..._h3_045`, the hay limits, the Newberry leads, the land-sale ground index, the asset manifests and the two GLBs per roof. NOTHING IS ADJUDICATED HERE: every family below is the `to_family` T-1445 reached and every reason beside it is T-1445's own, quoted. The parcel still builds 60 roofs at the same coordinates, rotations and clusters. What moves is which family stands where, THREE FOOTPRINTS that the family they join cannot carry at the depth they had --- `..._c2_027` 20x32 to 20x30 ft, `..._w1_018` 18x28 to 18x27 ft, and `..._h3_045` 32x48 to the 30x42 ft ceiling of the H2 band --- and ONE INVENTORY CLASS: `..._c1_047` is moved from a store to a stable and a stable is ancillary, so the parcel's mix is recounted from 45/15 to 44/16 rather than the class being held to keep an old total. Three yards named after a migrated roof are renamed with it. Everything here is still conjectural exactly as it was --- that any building stood on this ground, which building it was, and every dimension of it. Recorded in docs/LIBERTIES.md.

kinzie_street_trade.why: THE NORTH DIVISION'S TRADE ROOFS GO BACK TO THE STREET THE MEMO NAMES FOR THEM. The order book owes the North three stores, one inn or tavern and two workshops (`structures/{stores_mixed_use,inns_taverns,workshops}/north`, T-1205's rows), and they are owed because T-1480 refamilied seven of this recipe's own trade roofs as dwellings when T-1445 found them standing 9 to 48 m back from any street line. The 665-roof schedule then dealt their families to blk_indiana_north_wolcott and blk_indiana_north_cass in Kinzie's Addition, where the block generator refuses every one of them: Wolcott is graded `light`, Indiana, Illinois and Cass `none`, and no store, warehouse or workshop stands on either grade. Kinzie Street is graded `ordinary`, its north face was empty on the street line from Clark Street to east of Wolcott, and `docs/RESEARCH/1835_north_division_extent_and_infill.md` names the Wolcott-Kinzie core as the strongest north cluster for exactly that combination of river approach and street. So the six stand there, fronting Kinzie (bearing 180), each front wall about 0.6 m clear of the Kinzie corridor on its control line (the drawn line runs 2.91 m south of it; AGENTS.md rule 10), with open ground between every pair: the memo's alternation of roof and open yard, not a street wall. The T1 is the nearest to the Dearborn drawbridge approach, which is where the lodging clause puts an inn; the C4 and a C3 take the two Kinzie corners of Wolcott. Every value is reconstructed and none is a reading of a source about these buildings (L368).

deferred.why: The North Water bank is where a forwarding warehouse would stand and it is the one north street the committed hierarchy grades `light`; the commercial-front clause avoids light streets and the block generator refuses a store, warehouse or workshop on one. Seating it needs a bank-landing clause or a regrade of North Water argued on its own evidence, which is a separate question from this deal, so it is left owed rather than forced onto Kinzie Street.

addition_surplus.why: THE MEMO STANDS AND THE SEATING GIVES WAY: THE ADDITION'S 26 DWELLINGS COME SOUTH OF MICHIGAN STREET. The order book owes the North 26 ordinary dwellings (`structures/ordinary_dwellings/north`: target 84, standing 58), and the 665-roof schedule had dealt every one of them to Kinzie's Addition's two subdivided blocks, 20 to blk_indiana_north_wolcott (D2 2, D3 2, D4 6, D5 5, D6 3, D7 2) and 6 to blk_indiana_north_cass (D2, D3, D4 and D6 one each, D5 two). Both blocks already stand at the ceiling docs/RESEARCH/1835_north_division_extent_and_infill.md puts on them, four roofs each with open ground on both sides of every one (L294), and the three other lotted cells of the Addition are apportioned none (T-1757). So one of the two had to move. The memo does not: it is this project's committed reading of the July 1835 north side (a large platted addition with no buildings drawn on it, kept visibly speculative), and the seating is a policy deal that reads no source about these blocks. Nor does the memo refuse the roofs themselves: its own full North target is 90 ordinary dwellings against the 84 the inventory asks, and what it refuses is spending them north of Michigan Street. So the 26 stand, family for family as the schedule dealt them, in the memo's three inner clusters: a loose run along the north face of Kinzie Street west of Dearborn and east of Wolcott (Kinzie between Dearborn and Wolcott is left as T-1205 dealt it, with no house between its trade roofs), a few on the south face of Kinzie in the North Water band, and the rest scattered through the Kinzie-Michigan interior with Michigan Street left a sparse outer edge. Each centre was chosen by a deterministic search against the generator's own predicates and three more, all measured at the deal: no platted corridor on its drawn line, dry covered ground with no more than 0.35 m of relief, at least 14 m from every committed roof (an open yard between every pair, never a street wall), at least 25 m from every named structure (the recipe's review buffer), and inside the initial occupied envelope (E 430-1300, N 105-390). Every value is reconstructed and none is a reading of a source about these houses (L391).
